title: A day with a zookeeper
text:
Anna Kowalska is 34 and she works at a zoo. She looks after the giraffes and zebras. We asked her about her job.

What time does your day start?
I start work at 7 a.m. First, I check all the animals. I look at their eyes, legs and skin to see if they are healthy. Then I clean their houses. It's not the nicest part of the job, but it's very important.

What do the animals eat?
Giraffes eat leaves, hay and vegetables. A giraffe can eat about 30 kilos of food a day! In summer, visitors can feed them in the afternoon, but only with special food from us.

What do you like most about your job?
Every animal has its own personality. Our oldest giraffe, Mira, is very calm, but the young ones are curious and sometimes naughty. I love watching them.

Is there anything you don't like?
Winter is hard. I work outside in the cold and the rain. And I don't have much time for holidays – the animals need us every day.

What do you need to become a zookeeper?
You need to love animals, of course, and you need to be strong and patient. Most zookeepers study biology or work as volunteers first.
